note: LOCAL_IPC_AND_DEVICE_IDENTITY.md states that role confusion and stale handshakes are rejected. Before PF-012 the protocol had neither a shape that made role confusion unrepresentable nor a reason code with which to refuse it: Envelope carried one universal oneof holding every body, and sender_role was a field the sender filled in. These vectors state the two refusals the document already promised, so a case fails by disagreeing rather than by being absent.

cases.title: same-user impersonation

given.peer_uid: same as the daemon's own uid

cases.note: The attacker runs as the same user, so uid alone proves nothing — every role in local-trust-domains-v1.json runs per-user and shares that uid. The executable identity is what separates them: SecCode on macOS, the Authenticode publisher plus service SID on Windows, and the resolved /proc/pid/exe on Linux. A check that stopped at SO_PEERCRED uid would accept this.

cases.title: stale process after a role grant is reissued

given.peer_uid: same as the daemon's own uid

cases.action: resume an established connection and send source_observation_submission
cases.note: A genuine collector from before a daemon restart or a revocation. Its executable identity verifies and its grant does not. Without a generation the daemon cannot tell a survivor from a current peer, which is what makes revocation meaningful rather than advisory.

cases.title: role confusion is unrepresentable, not merely refused
cases.action: encode a deletion request inside the collector arm
cases.note: CollectorToDaemon has no local_deletion_request arm, so this cannot be encoded at all. The case is retained because a sender may still set sender_role to one role and select another role's arm on the envelope, which remains detectable and is what this code names.

cases.title: the supervisor cannot read a queue
cases.action: encode a queue summary request inside the supervisor arm
cases.note: The elevated role has the narrowest surface: health and lifecycle only. This is the case where the universal oneof was most dangerous, because a compromised supervisor could previously encode any message in the protocol while running as root.

cases.title: a well-formed collector submission is accepted
cases.note: The positive case. Without it the four refusals above are satisfied by a channel that refuses everything.
